newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves into the banking system through a round of multi-day system repurchase agreements Thursday, analysts said.

Analysts said the projected $6.0 billion add need in the two-week maintenance period, which begins Thursday, insures the Fed will enter the market. The Fed will add via four-, six-, eight-, or 14-day system RPs, most agreeed.
The Fed is also expected to make an outright purchase of coupons as early as this session.
Should the Fed only do four-day system RPs, that would suggest the Fed would begin buying coupons Thursday or Friday.

Still, analysts are leaning toward after Thanksgiving for a pass. James Blumenthal, money market economist at MCM MoneyWatch, noted that the Fed has bought coupons in eight straight Novembers, but after Thanksgiving in six of those years.
Therefore, adds J.P. Morgan & Co Fed watcher Marc Wanshel, the Fed will likely just do eight-day system RPs, which would add reserves through the holiday.
